premise: Each row is one choice the owner can make. A row is only complete when it names what would settle it. Where no official document settles the question, sources is empty, evidence_status is 'unverified', and the page says so instead of citing something that does not answer the question.
rules: sources[] must contain IDs registered in data/sources.json. The build fails on an unregistered ID.
A row with sources: [] must set evidence_status: 'unverified'. tools/check_site.py enforces both halves.
No effort estimate here is a time promise; effort is a relative band (S = one session, M = a focused day, L = a project).

decisions.title: Make every outbound product link a tagged Special Link, or keep the supplied short links
decisions.why: Amazon's Program Policies require an Associates ID or tag as a parameter in the URL of each link to an Amazon site. The five supplied link.amazon short links carry no visible tag in the URL a reader receives, and the enrolled-account test has not been run.
decisions.recommendation: Owner runs one signed-in click per product through SiteStripe, confirms the destination and that a click is reported, then replaces the hrefs with the tagged links if the report works. Do not describe the supplied short links as invalid; their status is unresolved, not disproven.
decisions.blocks: Any traffic push. A click that is not tagged earns nothing.

decisions.title: Show prices from the Product Advertising API, or keep showing none
decisions.why: Program Policies 2(b) allow price and availability only when Amazon serves the data or it arrives through the Creators/PA API. The site currently shows none, which is compliant and costs conversion.
decisions.recommendation: Stay with no prices until the account qualifies for the API, then show API-served prices with the required attribution. Anything else means publishing numbers that are wrong within hours.
decisions.blocks: The strongest single conversion lever on the site.

decisions.title: Turn on Search Console, or keep choosing topics by instinct
decisions.why: No query data exists for this site. Every topic decision so far has been editorial judgement. Search Console is free and takes about ten minutes once.
decisions.recommendation: Verify the property this week and submit sitemap.xml. From then on, the next guide is chosen from measured queries and not from taste.
decisions.blocks: The answer to 'which guide should be ninth'. Without it, any answer is a guess.

decisions.title: Use Amazon-served product images, or keep the typographic cards
decisions.why: The site uses illustrated cards built from each product's own numbers, because using listing photography means relying on Amazon's Program Content licence, which is granted for Amazon marketing and can be terminated.
decisions.recommendation: Keep the typographic cards for now. They are honest, they carry the key spec, and they avoid a licensing dependency this site cannot police. Revisit only if a reader test shows the cards cost clicks.
decisions.blocks: Nothing. The current state is safe.

decisions.title: Buy one unit of each family to earn first-hand testing, or stay a documentation desk
decisions.why: Every number on this site is a seller statement. That is disclosed everywhere, but it caps how much authority the writing can carry, and Google's people-first guidance rewards demonstrable experience.
decisions.recommendation: Two units — one air fryer, one thermometer — would let the site publish its own measurements and stop qualifying every sentence. That is a spend decision, not an editorial one.
decisions.blocks: The difference between 'here is what the label says' and 'here is what we measured'.

decisions.title: Cut the list to one product family, or keep air fryers and thermometers together
decisions.why: Five products across two families read as two separate sites sharing a header. The current framing — cooking to a target temperature — is defensible but it is doing real work to hold the set together.
decisions.recommendation: Keep both for now, but make the air fryers the spine and treat the thermometers as the smaller shelf. If one family earns no traffic after a quarter of Search Console data, retire it.
decisions.blocks: Any brand or navigation decision that assumes a single beat.

decisions.title: Ship a self-hosted analytics endpoint, or keep measurement local-only
decisions.why: GitHub Pages cannot receive POSTs, so any server-side counter needs a separate service. Five event types are defined and four are emitted, but nothing is transmitted today.
decisions.recommendation: Choose the endpoint and its retention period before writing anything else that assumes traffic data. Until then, the local-only counter is honest and useful only to the reader.
decisions.blocks: Every claim about which page or product is working.

decisions.title: Add a reader email list, or stay RSS-only
decisions.why: There is no mailing list, so there is no form. An unconnected form with a fake confirmation would be worse than none.
decisions.recommendation: Stay RSS-only until there is a provider and a consent sentence the owner is willing to stand behind. A newsletter that never sends is a broken promise.
decisions.blocks: Reader capture, and any plan that depends on repeat visits.

decisions.title: Keep the site on the github.io project path, or move to a custom domain
decisions.why: Every canonical, sitemap entry and social card currently points at wingbangboozle1-lang.github.io/Prod3/. A domain move rewrites all of them and any existing links break unless redirected.
decisions.recommendation: Decide before any promotion. After promotion, the move costs whatever links have accumulated. On a project path, hosting stays free and the URL stays slightly awkward.
decisions.blocks: Brand decisions, and any print or social material carrying the URL.

decisions.title: Publish on a fixed cadence, or publish when a guide is ready
decisions.why: Eight guides shipped in one pass and nothing since. A cadence that nobody owns is a wish with a calendar attached.
decisions.recommendation: One guide a month, chosen from Search Console once it is verified, with the owner named as the person who approves it. Monthly is survivable; weekly is not, for one person.
decisions.blocks: Whether this is a publication or a finished project.

paths.name: Make it earn
paths.summary: Fix the links and the measurement first, then write. Nothing new is published until a click can be counted.
includes: DT-01: one signed-in Special Link test per product
DT-07: choose and stand up the analytics endpoint
DT-03: Search Console verified, sitemap submitted
Then one guide, chosen from search data
paths.cost: One session for the link test, one focused day for the endpoint
paths.best_if: The goal is revenue in the next ninety days.

paths.name: Make it a publication
paths.summary: Buy the two units, publish real measurements, and let first-hand testing carry the writing.
includes: DT-05: one air fryer and one thermometer purchased
Test notes and measured temperatures published as method
A named author with a stated basis for the claim
Cadence fixed at one guide a month
delays: Costs money before it earns any
paths.cost: Purchase price of two units, plus a recurring writing commitment
paths.best_if: The goal is a site that ranks and is worth reading in a year.

paths.name: Narrow and harden
paths.summary: Keep air fryers, retire the thermometer shelf, and resolve every owner-only question before adding anything.
includes: DT-06: air fryers as the single beat
DT-09: settle the URL before promoting it
Clear the owner-only question rows (Q-02, Q-03, Q-04, Q-18, Q-19)
No new content until the desk is empty
delays: The thermometer guides lose their home
paths.cost: Mostly time, and one irreversible-ish pruning decision
paths.best_if: The site is a side project that must stay small and correct.
